analysis.title: EcoFlash: Central banks: a pause while waiting for more information
key_insights: The Fed, ECB and BoJ all left rates unchanged this week, as expected. BNP says the pause does not mark the end of the tightening cycle.

ECB statement is more balanced than September. It now cites both upside inflation risks (size and persistence of the energy shock) and downside pressure from tighter financial conditions. The phrase that inflation would stay 'well above target for an extended period' was dropped.
BNP's base case is one final ECB rate hike in December. Lagarde implicitly signaled it: 'If the current situation is not called into question by the next set of economic data, the path is clear'.

Lagarde described higher sovereign yields as a global phenomenon that is tightening financial conditions. On the TPI, the ECB will intervene only if transmission is hampered 'by disorderly movements not justified by fundamentals'.

Euro area September producer prices show clearer signals, but the increase is limited to energy, electricity-intensive industries and electrical equipment. Eurozone companies, especially in services, appear to be absorbing the energy shock. The European Commission survey shows the October sales price index rising in line with recent months.

The FOMC held the funds target at 3.75%-4.0% after September's hike. Chair Kevin Warsh described stronger growth, a 'rather positive' labor market and inflation that is 'too high'. Two of 12 voters dissented in favor of a 25bp hike.

Warsh warned that an abrupt tightening could hurt the AI investment cycle, and the comment steepened the yield curve. He will attend a 'Productivity and Employment' task force hearing on Nov 16 to refine his views on AI and the dual mandate.
The Fed will hold fewer rate-decision meetings: 7 in 2027 and 6 in 2028, versus 8 today, starting in fall 2027. The freed meetings are for 'strategic deliberations' and long-term issues.
The BoJ held its policy rate at 1.25% on Oct 29-30, in line with BNP and consensus. One member dissented in favor of a 25bp hike, versus two dovish dissents at the previous meeting.

The BoJ said core inflation 'has reached a level generally in line with price stability' and is expected to remain there. Ueda said inflation must be 'anchored' there before the target is declared achieved. The BoJ's emphasis on upside price risks and its view that higher core inflation is 'undesirable' signal continued tightening.

BNP says the next steps are likely larger in the US, where inflation has exceeded target for nearly six years alongside a favorable growth and jobs outlook. Eurozone inflation is mainly an energy supply shock with little effect on core measures, and households' long-term inflation expectations remain anchored.

Real policy rates differ across the three banks. The ECB deposit rate deflated by core CPI is around 0%, near estimates of the natural rate. The Fed's real rate (funds rate deflated by core PCE) is about 0.8%, 40bp below the committee's implied long-run level of 1.2%. Japan's real rates are still negative.

BNP forecasts one final ECB hike in December, two Fed hikes (December and January) and four spaced-out BoJ hikes through the second half of 2028. The BoJ cycle should end at the upper end of its 1.1%-2.5% neutral range estimate.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held after September's hike. Two dissenters wanted another 25bp, so the risk to the next move is toward more tightening.
The BoJ held, with one hawkish dissent. BNP expects tightening to continue gradually.

tension_points.bull_case: Warsh cites stronger growth, a 'rather positive' labor market and inflation 'too high'. Two dissenters wanted a 25bp hike now, and BNP expects hikes in December and January.
tension_points.bear_case: The committee fears the adverse effects of tightening too quickly, including on the AI investment cycle, and a credit shock, so it is waiting to 'accumulate more information'.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Warsh said the committee is waiting to accumulate more information. The report names no specific level or print.
